```{r libraries and data}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(stats)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(forcats)


hcmd <- readRDS("~/Documents/GitHub/harmonized_carceral_mortality_data/data/hcmd.rds")

```

Timing of deaths Figure: Mean + StDev (dot and whisker) of Deaths by Month across all years (x axis is month, y axis is # of deaths)

```{r timingofdeaths}

monthly_summary <- hcmd %>%
  count(year, death_month, name = "deaths") %>%
  group_by(death_month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_deaths = mean(deaths),
    sd_deaths = sd(deaths),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    death_month = factor(month.abb[death_month], levels = month.abb)
  )

monthly_summary$death_month <- factor(
  monthly_summary$death_month,
  levels = month.abb
)

dotandwhisker<-ggplot(monthly_summary, aes(x = death_month, y = mean_deaths)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_deaths - sd_deaths,
                    ymax = mean_deaths + sd_deaths),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Number of Deaths",
    title = "Mean Monthly Deaths Across Years (1996-2024)"
  ) +
  theme_classic()


```


##summary of state data completeness 
```{r summarizing data}
combined<-hcmd

#checking how many states are represented , finding out all states are
statetable<-combined%>%group_by(state_abbrev)%>%count()

#checking out how many unique facilities are represented, 1089 are 
facilitiestable<-combined%>%group_by(hifld_facility_id)%>%count()

#reorganizing death date as a Date str 
str(combined$death_date_dt)

combined$death_date_dt<-as.Date(combined$death_date_dt)

str(combined$death_date_dt)

#comparing # of mortality records across years 
combined<-combined%>%mutate(year=year(death_date_dt))

deaths_by_year<-combined%>%group_by(year)%>%count()

#checking out years of coverage by state
coverage <- combined %>%
  group_by(state_abbrev) %>%
  summarize(
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


#plotting from earliest to latest beginning of coverage
ggplot(combined, aes(x =year, y = fct_reorder(state_abbrev, year, .fun = min, .desc = TRUE))) +
  geom_tile(fill = "black", width = 1, height = 0.75) + 
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1996, 2024, by = 4)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),     
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),       
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "lightgray"), 
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Temporal Coverage of Incarcerated Mortality Data by State", 
    x = "Year", 
    y = "State"
  )

#plotting by least to most coverage
combined2 <- combined %>%
  left_join(coverage, by = "state_abbrev")

ggplot(
  combined2,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = fct_reorder(state_abbrev, n_years, .desc = TRUE)
  )
) +
  geom_tile(fill = "black", width = 1, height = 0.75) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1996, 2024, by = 4)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "lightgray"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "State"
  )
```

##summarizing across time (2013-2019 according to the plot)
```{r summarizingtime}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

states20132019<- combined %>% filter(year >=2013 & year<=2019)%>%group_by(state_abbrev)%>%summarize(years_covered = n_distinct(year))%>%filter(years_covered==7)%>%pull(state_abbrev)
  
filtered_states <- combined %>%
  filter(state_abbrev %in% states20132019) %>% filter(year >=2013 & year<=2019)

yearly_comparison <- filtered_states %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(total_records = n())
```

#by climate region
```{r climateregion}

climateregions <- combined %>%
  mutate(
    climate_region = case_when(
      state_abbrev %in% c("CT", "DE", "ME", "MD", "MA", "NH", "NJ", "NY", "PA", "RI", "VT") ~ "Northeast",
      state_abbrev %in% c("IA", "MI", "MN", "WI")                                         ~ "Upper Midwest",
      state_abbrev %in% c("IL", "IN", "KY", "MO", "OH", "TN", "WV")                       ~ "Ohio Valley",
      state_abbrev %in% c("AL", "FL", "GA", "NC", "SC", "VA")                             ~ "Southeast",
      state_abbrev %in% c("MT", "NE", "ND", "SD", "WY")                                   ~ "Northern Rockies and Plains",
      state_abbrev %in% c("AR", "KS", "LA", "MS", "OK", "TX")                             ~ "South",
      state_abbrev %in% c("AZ", "CO", "NM", "UT")                                         ~ "Southwest",
      state_abbrev %in% c("ID", "OR", "WA")                                               ~ "Northwest",
      state_abbrev %in% c("CA", "NV")                                                     ~ "West",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown/Other"
    )
  )


region_analysis <- climateregions %>%
  group_by(climate_region) %>% 
  summarise(
    earliest_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_deaths  = n()  # This counts the actual rows/deaths in each region
  )
            
```

#stacked bar chart 
```{r barchart}
library(readxl)
output <- read_excel("code/cod_algorithm/b_02_full_results_ICD.xlsx")

output%>%count(class)

top4 <- output %>% 
  count(CLASS_LEVEL_3, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 4) %>%
  pull(CLASS_LEVEL_3)

barchart <- output %>%
  mutate(
    cause = if_else(CLASS_LEVEL_3 %in% top4,
                    CLASS_LEVEL_3,
                    "All Other")
  ) %>%
  count(cause) %>%
  mutate(cause = fct_reorder(cause, n))

ggplot(barchart,
       aes(x = cause, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4472C4") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Mortality Records"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)





```

#age and sex
```{r ageandsex}
combined_age_sex<-combined%>%
  mutate(sex= case_when(
  sex == -1 ~ NA ,
  sex == 1 ~ "Male",
  sex == 2 ~ "Female"),
  age_group = case_when(
    age<= 44 ~ "< 45", 
    age > 44 & age<= 58 ~ "45 - 58",
    age > 58 & age <= 66 ~ "59 - 66",
    age >= 67 ~ ">67",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))


combined_age_sex%>%group_by(sex)%>%count()


#total with data= 39944 (80.4%).

#3.7% female
#96.3% male 

combined_age_sex%>%group_by(age_group)%>%count()



```
